nodes.summary: Holm's procedure at level `α ≥ 0` rejects exactly `holmIndex α p` hypotheses.
nodes.title: Number of hypotheses rejected by Holm's procedure

nodes.summary: If Holm rejects a hypothesis in `J`, then some `j ∈ J` has p-value at most `α / |J|`: the first hypothesis of `J` in sorted order sits at a position `k ≤ m - |J| + 1`. This is the shared Holm rejection bound, used both for Holm's FWER control below and for identifying Holm's procedure with the closure of the Bonferroni local tests.
nodes.title: Holm rejection bound for a set of hypotheses

nodes.summary: Holm's step-down count is at most `m`.
nodes.title: Holm's step-down count is at most the number of tests

nodes.summary: Holm's step-down count at level `α`: the largest `r ∈ {0, …, m}` such that for every `k ∈ {1, …, r}` the `k`-th smallest p-value is at most `α / (m - k + 1)`, i.e. at least `k` p-values are at most `α / (m - k + 1)`. (`r = 0` always qualifies.)
nodes.title: Holm's step-down count

nodes.summary: The hypotheses rejected by Holm's step-down procedure at level `α`: those whose p-value is at most `α / (m - r + 1)` with `r = holmIndex α p`; these are the hypotheses with the `r` smallest p-values.
nodes.title: Hypotheses rejected by Holm's step-down procedure

nodes.summary: Holm's count is the largest index up to which every step succeeds.
nodes.title: Holm's count is the largest index where every step succeeds

nodes.summary: Every step up to Holm's count succeeds: for `1 ≤ k ≤ holmIndex α p`, at least `k` p-values are at most `α / (m - k + 1)`.
nodes.title: Every step up to Holm's count succeeds

nodes.summary: If every true-null p-value is valid, the probability that Holm's step-down procedure at level `α ∈ [0, 1]` rejects at least one true null is at most `α`. No independence is assumed.
nodes.title: Holm's procedure controls the FWER

nodes.summary: The rejection set is closed under smaller p-values.
nodes.title: Holm's rejection set is closed under smaller p-values

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
